_README: Each mutation breaks ONE behaviour the fixture claims to cover. Aim them at distinct branches — a mutation that neuters the whole hook only proves the suite notices a corpse. `why` is printed in the run output, so write it as the thing that would be silently broken. A key names the file to mutate, resolved the same way run-fixtures resolves a hook. Add "suite": "<hook>" when the mutated file is a shared library, so the run exercises a suite that actually consumes it.

destructive-guard.why: a substitution in a cd stops making the directory unresolvable, so `cd "$(dirname <main>/x)" && git push` reads the session's branch
an escaped space resolves to a missing directory again, so `cd main\ wt && git push` reads the session's branch
a cd behind if/then/do/builtin/command/time stops moving the directory
a case pattern's `)` closes a subshell again, so a later bare push reads the parent directory
every `)` closes a subshell again, so `$((1+1))` pops the directory a cd set
pushd stops moving the directory, so `pushd <main> && git push` reads the session's branch
--git-dir and GIT_DIR= stop naming the repository, so `git --git-dir=<main>/.git push` reads the session's branch
--recurse-submodules stops consuming its value, so `git push --recurse-submodules check origin` reads `check` as the remote
a tags-only push defaults to HEAD again, so `git push origin --tags` from main hard-blocks
an unreadable destination stops standing for the checked-out branch, so `git push origin $(git branch --show-current)` from main passes
a separator glued to a force or delete flag hides it again, so `git push origin x -f;echo` skips the prompt
a colon refspec after the first counts as no delete, so `git push origin x :other` skips the prompt
a subshell's last word inside a case arm reads as a pattern again, so `case x in x) (cd <feature>; true); git push;; esac` keeps the subshell's directory
`esac)` reads as a case pattern again, so a subshell wrapped around a case never closes
an escaped parenthesis counts as a subshell boundary again, so `(cd <main>; echo a\)b; git push)` pops early
the toplevel idiom becomes unresolvable again, so `cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" && git push -u origin HEAD` blocks from a feature checkout
an exported GIT_DIR stops moving the repository, so `export GIT_DIR=<main>/.git && git push` reads the session's branch
a bare GIT_DIR= assignment stops making the repository unknown, so `GIT_DIR=<main>/.git; git push` reads the session's branch
unset GIT_DIR stops restoring the directory's repository, so `export GIT_DIR=<main>/.git; unset GIT_DIR; git push` blocks from a feature checkout
an export with no value stops making the repository unknown, so `export GIT_DIR && git push` reads the session's branch
an abbreviated long option stops naming its option, so `git push --recu check origin` from main reads `check` as the remote
a bundled -o stops taking its value, so `git push -uo ci.skip origin` from main reads `ci.skip` as the remote
a force refspec with `~`, `^` or `@` stops asking, so `git push origin +HEAD~1:feature` rewinds the remote unprompted
pushd -n reads `-n` as a directory again, so `pushd -n <main> && git push` from a feature checkout hard-blocks
a quote glued to the verb stops counting it, so `bash -c 'git push"" origin main'` reads no push

cd stops skipping `--`, so `cd <main> && cd -- && git push` reads `--` as a directory and hard-blocks instead of going home

a push anywhere after git counts again, so `git stash push -m wip` on a main checkout hard-blocks
checkout or switch anywhere after git counts again, so `git -C <main> grep -n checkout` blocks as a branch switch
branch moves stop being recorded, so `git checkout main && git push` from a feature checkout passes
a checkout of a ref with paths counts as a branch move, so `git checkout main README.txt && git push` blocks
a worktree the command adds stops carrying its branch, so a push from a new -b worktree hard-blocks
a directory the command makes falls back to the session branch, so a bare push there reads the session's
a subshell's export leaks again, so `cd <main> && (export GIT_DIR=<feature>/.git); git push` passes
a substitution's export leaks again, so `x=$(export GIT_DIR=<feature>/.git); git push` passes

only the first push in a shell string is read again, so `bash -c "git push origin x && git push origin main"` passes
escaped quotes in a shell string stay escaped, so `bash -c "git push origin \"main\""` passes
a glued -o value takes the next word again, so `git push -oo origin main` reads `main` as the remote
